evidence.reference_title: HSF4 Transcriptionally Activates Autophagy by Regulating ATG9a During Lens Terminal Differentiation.
evidence.snippet: Our study indicates that autophagy activation is a possible therapeutic strategy for HSF4-related congenital cataracts.

nodes.description: Removal of a visually significant opacified lens with optical correction and amblyopia therapy is the standard management of early-onset cataract. No HSF4-directed therapy exists.

HSF4 directly activates ATG9A (mainly the lens ATG9a-X2 isoform). HSF4del42 mouse lenses show delayed clearance of mitochondria, ER and Golgi and impaired autophagic flux; rapamycin partly restores clearance.

evidence.reference_title: HSF4 Transcriptionally Activates Autophagy by Regulating ATG9a During Lens Terminal Differentiation.
evidence.snippet: HSF4 directly transcriptionally activated the core autophagy protein ATG9a.

nodes.description: HSF4 binds the DLAD (DNASE2B) promoter and drives the DNase that degrades nuclear DNA in maturing fibers. Mutant HSF4 fails to induce DLAD, and HSF4 knockdown in zebrafish leaves fiber nuclei incompletely degraded.

animal_models.name: hsf4-null zebrafish

biological_processes: lens fiber cell nuclear DNA degradation

evidence.reference_title: HSF4 regulates DLAD expression and promotes lens de-nucleation.
evidence.snippet: These results were confirmed by HSF4 knockdown in zebrafish, which led to incomplete de-nucleation of the lens and decreased expression and activity of DLAD.

evidence.reference_title: HSF4 regulates DLAD expression and promotes lens de-nucleation.
evidence.snippet: In this study, we found that HSF4 promoted the expression and DNase activity of DLAD by directly binding to the DLAD promoter.

nodes.description: HSF4 stabilizes nuclear p53 and induces p21, FAS and BAX, promoting G1/S arrest of lens epithelial cells and their transition to fiber cells. Cataract-causing mutants lose this activity; HSF4-deficient mouse and fish lenses show epithelial overproliferation and disordered fibers.
nodes.id: Failure of p53-Dependent Lens Epithelial Cell Cycle Exit

animal_models.description: Lens epithelial cells overproliferate and differentiate prematurely.
animal_models.name: Hsf4 knockout mouse

evidence.reference_title: HSF4 promotes G1/S arrest in human lens epithelial cells by stabilizing p53.
evidence.snippet: In contrast, HSF4 with cataract causative mutations fail to cause cell cycle arrest and have no obvious effect on cell proliferation.

evidence.reference_title: HSF4 is required for normal cell growth and differentiation during mouse lens development.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, we found increased proliferation and premature differentiation of the mutant lens epithelial cells, which is associated with increased expression of growth factors, FGF-1, FGF-4, and FGF-7.

evidence.reference_title: HSF4 regulates lens fiber cell differentiation by activating p53 and its downstream regulators.
evidence.snippet: The epithelial cells of the lens were overproliferated, resulting in the overabundance of lens fiber cells in hsf4null zebrafish lens.

evidence.reference_title: Mutant DNA-binding domain of HSF4 is associated with autosomal dominant lamellar and Marner cataract.
evidence.snippet: We suggest that HSF4 is critical to lens development.

evidence.reference_title: A novel HSF4 gene mutation (p.R405X) causing autosomal recessive congenital cataracts in a large consanguineous family from Pakistan.
evidence.snippet: The disease phenotype perfectly co-segregated with markers flanking the known cataract gene HSF4, whereas other autosomal recessive loci were excluded.

evidence.reference_title: HSF4 mutation p.Arg116His found in age-related cataracts and in normal populations produces childhood lamellar cataract in transgenic mice.
evidence.snippet: Here, we demonstrate via BAC (bacterial artificial chromosome) transgenesis that p.Arg116His recreates the childhood lamellar cataract in mice suggesting that incomplete penetrance associated with early cataracts may not be an absence but a limitation of the detection of the phenotype.

nodes.description: Recessive alleles (c.595_599del, p.Arg405*, c.1327+4A>G) produce proteins lacking C-terminal activation and repression domains. The mutant proteins are stable and nuclear, but none activates a heat shock element reporter.

evidence.reference_title: Functional analysis of HSF4 mutations found in patients with autosomal recessive congenital cataracts.
evidence.snippet: The three HSF4 autosomal recessive mutations evaluated here result in a loss of HSF4 function due to a loss of regulatory domains present at the C-terminal end.

evidence.reference_title: Functional analysis of HSF4 mutations found in patients with autosomal recessive congenital cataracts.
evidence.snippet: HSF4 mutant proteins did not differ in the protein turnover rate when compared with WT HSF4.

nodes.description: Dominant disease alleles are missense substitutions clustered in the N-terminal DNA-binding domain. Five congenital-cataract substitutions tested biochemically inhibited HSF4 DNA binding; because HSF4 acts as a trimer, a mutant subunit is proposed to interfere with the wild-type protein.

evidence.reference_title: DNA-binding and transcriptional activities of human HSF4 containing mutations that associate with congenital and age-related cataracts.
evidence.snippet: Five missense mutations that have been associated with congenital cataract inhibited DNA-binding of HSF4, which demonstrates the relationship between HSF4 mutations, loss of lens protein gene expression, and cataractogenesis.

evidence.reference_title: A novel missense mutation in HSF4 causes autosomal-dominant congenital lamellar cataract in a British family.
evidence.snippet: This mutation is likely to be dominant negative and affect the DNA-binding affinity of HSF4.

nodes.id: Hsf4 DNA-binding domain-EGFP BAC transgenic mouse

nodes.description: Lamellar (zonular) opacity is the defining presentation of the dominant DNA-binding-domain alleles in Chinese and British families.

evidence.reference_title: Mutant DNA-binding domain of HSF4 is associated with autosomal dominant lamellar and Marner cataract.
evidence.snippet: We carried out whole-genome linkage analysis of Chinese individuals with lamellar cataract, and found that the disorder is associated with inheritance of a 5.11-cM locus on chromosome 16.

evidence.reference_title: A novel missense mutation in HSF4 causes autosomal-dominant congenital lamellar cataract in a British family.
evidence.snippet: We have identified a novel mutation in HSF4 in a large British pedigree causing dominant congenital lamellar cataract.

nodes.description: Lens opacity beginning at birth or in early childhood, usually bilateral, with morphology varying within and between families (lamellar, zonular, nuclear, stellate, anterior polar, total).

evidence.reference_title: Expression of the HSF4 DNA binding domain-EGFP hybrid gene recreates early childhood lamellar cataract in transgenic mice.
evidence.snippet: We recapitulated the human lamellar cataract, in its temporal as well as spatial presentation, within the transgenic mouse lens.

nodes.description: Marner cataract, described in a large Danish pedigree, is mainly zonular, with stellate and anterior polar components in some relatives. The cited abstract states only the association with HSF4; the morphology is from the deep-research summary of the original pedigree.

evidence.reference_title: Mutant DNA-binding domain of HSF4 is associated with autosomal dominant lamellar and Marner cataract.
evidence.snippet: We also discovered an association between a missense mutation and Marner cataract in an extensive Danish family.

nodes.description: HSF4 directly activates lens structural genes (gamma-crystallins including gammaS, and the beaded filament genes BFSP1 and BFSP2), the lysosomal DNase DLAD (DNASE2B), the autophagy gene ATG9A, and stabilizes p53 to induce p21, FAS and BAX. Loss of HSF4 activity reduces each of these outputs; the nodes below follow the separate branches.

biological_processes: positive regulation of transcription by HSF4

evidence.reference_title: DNA-binding and transcriptional activities of human HSF4 containing mutations that associate with congenital and age-related cataracts.
evidence.snippet: Here, we show that HSF4 activates transcription of genes encoding crystallins and beaded filament structural proteins in lens epithelial cells.

nodes.description: Hsf4-null mouse lenses show reduced gammaS-crystallin, Bfsp1 and Bfsp2 expression and loss of alphaA-crystallin modifications, with fiber cells carrying inclusion-like structures.
nodes.id: Reduced Lens Crystallin and Beaded Filament Expression

animal_models.name: Hsf4 knockout mouse

evidence.reference_title: Removal of Hsf4 leads to cataract development in mice through down-regulation of gamma S-crystallin and Bfsp expression.
evidence.snippet: Q-PCR analysis revealed down-regulation of several cataract-relevant genes, including gamma S-crystallin (Crygs) and lens-specific beaded filament proteins 1 and 2 (Bfsp1 and Bfsp2), in the lens of the Hsf4-/- mouse.

evidence.reference_title: HSF4 is required for normal cell growth and differentiation during mouse lens development.
evidence.snippet: HSF4-null mice had cataract with abnormal lens fiber cells containing inclusion-like structures, probably due to decreased expression of gamma-crystallin, which maintains protein stability.

nodes.description: Congenital total white cataract in the recessive Tunisian family. HPO has no current total-cataract term (HP:0010700 is obsolete, replaced by HP:0000518), so the developmental cataract term is bound.

evidence.reference_title: A homozygous splice mutation in the HSF4 gene is associated with an autosomal recessive congenital cataract.
evidence.snippet: DNA was extracted from blood samples from a large Tunisian family with an autosomal recessive, congenital, total white cataract.
